### Step 1 — Scene
Two small soft tacos with browned ground meat, shredded lettuce, diced tomato, shredded cheese, and a little red sauce.

### Step 2 — Vessel
A round dinner plate, approximately **26 cm diameter**.  
Plate area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

### Steps 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
Area shares allocate the food-covered footprint between ingredients to avoid double-counting overlapping layers. Heights are approximate average thicknesses.

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Soft tortillas | 22% | 117 × 0.40 = 47 ml | 0.95 | 44 g | 310 | 136 kcal |
| Cooked ground meat | 20% | 106 × 1.20 = 127 ml | 0.95 | 121 g | 270 | 327 kcal |
| Shredded lettuce | 6% | 32 × 1.60 = 51 ml | 0.15 | 8 g | 15 | 1 kcal |
| Diced tomato | 4% | 21 × 1.10 = 23 ml | 0.60 | 14 g | 18 | 3 kcal |
| Shredded cheese | 3% | 16 × 0.45 = 7 ml | 0.95 | 7 g | 400 | 28 kcal |
| Red sauce/salsa | 2% | 11 × 0.50 = 5 ml | 1.00 | 5 g | 40 | 2 kcal |

**Area check:** 22 + 20 + 6 + 4 + 3 + 2 = **57% food coverage**, consistent with the substantial empty rim.

### Step 8 — Sanity check
Approximately **199 g and 497 kcal** is plausible for two small, meat-heavy tacos with light vegetable and cheese toppings. The main uncertainties are tortilla thickness and meat fat content.
